text:
Amanda L: quick sync — thinking about adding a Contingency Orchestration panel to Console for automatic fallback policies. need to capture triggers, degrade modes, and an immutable audit trail. :thinking_face:
Kevin C: sounds good. main questions: which triggers do we ship by default? error-rate, tail-latency, quota-exceed? and how do we surface severity?
Sara M: default set should be: 5xx-rate windowed, p99 latency spike, and per-model token-usage throttle. include a metric threshold and a consecutive-window count. keep it small to avoid noise.
Mike R: agree. also need cooldown + min-duration so we don't flip-flop. suggest fields: `threshold`, `window_secs`, `min_active_secs`, `cooldown_secs`.
Julia S: from UX perspective we need a compact summary card showing active mode, reason, & who approved. also a link to playback (request examples) for forensic.
Amanda L: +1. audit requirements: immutable policy versions, who triggered automated fallback (system vs user), and a request-sample id linked to traces. retention policy tied to enterprise tier.
Kevin C: implementation question — store policy as JSON blob or normalized rows? blobs are flexible but hard to query for telemetry. normalized is better for searching triggers. what do others think?
Sara M: prefer normalized for telemetry and alerts. but allow a free-text `conditions` blob for advanced rules. we can maintain an index for common fields.
Mike R: ops concern: what about multi-model routing? fallback should be able to route to compatible model variant (quantized/cheaper) with transformation rules. we need a compatibility matrix check when creating policy.
Amanda L: good call. UX should show comma-separated compatible variants and warnings if none. we should also forbid fallback that violates data residency.
Julia S: mock request: can we show a before/after sample and the delta in token cost on the policy card? product loves that. :money_with_wings:
Kevin C: api debate: expose a POST /policies that accepts structured payload vs a UI-only wizard that emits a blob. I'd like both: structured API + blob for overrides. API should return version id and a preview simulation job id.
Sara M: simulation job is key. we must provide a dry-run where policy is evaluated against a sample window and returns estimated actions and false-positive risk score.
Mike R: cooldown logic again: also add a global circuit-breaker cap per-customer to stop cascading fallbacks across many routes.
Amanda L: ops-bot will report deployments. tagging ops channel optional. current plan: design -> API proto -> backend model -> telemetry hooks -> UI.
OpsBot: policy-deploy-bot: policy v3 deployed to staging (policy_id=pol-2021x). tests passed: schema, compatibility check, simulation run OK.
Julia S: can someone drop initial mockups in Figma? Sara or Kevin?
Kevin C: i'll sketch flows, will include: create -> simulate -> schedule -> enable -> audit view. sending link in a follow-up. :eyes:
Amanda L: ok let's capture action items: 1) Kevin sketch API + UI flow, 2) Sara define telemetry table schema and simulation output, 3) Mike define cooldown & global circuit rules, 4) Julia create audit card mockups. set review for Tue next week.
Mike R: one more - backend should tag requests with `x-contingency-mode` header during simulation and active fallbacks for easier trace filtering.
Sara M: ack. add telemetry events: `contingency.triggered`, `contingency.reverted`, `contingency.simulated` with fields: policy_version, reason, sample_request_id.
Amanda L: perfect. FYI internal doc: https://redwood.app/internal/contingency-guides (will add design constraints).
Julia S: :thumbsup: ready to mock.
Kevin C: follow-up thread with API proto soon.
Amanda L: thanks team — short sync done.
